subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should the Skill Workshop lifecycle contract live in OpenClaw core as a docs/test-owned reference, as an optional ClawHub or bundle artifact, or not be standardized yet?
rationale: The request is technically plausible but sets product and security direction for a high-sensitivity write path, and the repository vision favors both security hardening and keeping optional package surfaces out of core when possible.

options.title: OpenClaw-native reference contract
options.body: Add a docs/test-owned JSON or YAML contract plus invariant tests, explicitly reference-only and generated or checked against the existing Skill Workshop service.

options.title: External AISP or bundle artifact
options.body: Keep core unchanged and publish the AISP/AISOP artifact through ClawHub or a bundle-style package once the core invariants are documented enough to reference.

options.title: Do not standardize yet
options.body: Keep the current docs and tests as the contract for now, and revisit after concrete runtime-validation work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98069 settles.

recommendation.title: OpenClaw-native reference contract
recommendation.body: Add a docs/test-owned JSON or YAML contract plus invariant tests, explicitly reference-only and generated or checked against the existing Skill Workshop service.

likelyOwner.reason: shakkernerd has the strongest central Skill Workshop implementation history and is the best routing candidate for whether this should become a core contract or stay external.
